evals.name: create-forking-research-skill
evals.prompt: we've got a big monorepo and every time i ask you to figure out how some subsystem works, the search results eat my whole context. i want a skill that goes off and researches a topic on its own and comes back with a write-up
evals.expected_output: A skill using context: fork with an appropriate agent, whose body reads as an executable task rather than guidelines.
assertions: A SKILL.md was created on disk with YAML frontmatter that parses
The frontmatter sets `context: fork`, since the whole point is keeping search output out of the main conversation
The frontmatter sets `agent:` to a real agent type - one of `Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`, or a custom agent whose definition is also created in this run

If `agent: Explore` was chosen, the skill or response accounts for Explore being read-only and skipping CLAUDE.md; if a different agent was chosen, the response says why read-only exploration was insufficient
The body is written as an executable task the subagent can perform (imperative steps with a stated deliverable), not as guidelines or background knowledge with no action
The body names what the subagent should return and in what shape, since only its final summary reaches the main conversation

Every frontmatter key is one of: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, context, agent, background, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, model, effort, paths, hooks, shell, disallowed-tools
No frontmatter key is present that the response never justifies - in particular `model`, `effort`, `paths`, or `hooks` appear only with a stated reason

evals.name: create-user-invoked-skill-with-script
evals.prompt: make me a skill for cutting a release - it needs to bump the version in package.json, regenerate the changelog from the commits since the last tag, and tag it. i don't want you firing that off on your own, only when i ask for it. the version bump logic is fiddly so it should be a real script rather than instructions you follow each time
evals.expected_output: A user-invoked skill with a bundled, executable script referenced via ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} and a matching allowed-tools rule.
assertions: A SKILL.md was created on disk with YAML frontmatter that parses
`disable-model-invocation: true` is set, because the user explicitly asked that it never fire on its own
An executable script file was created under the skill's `scripts/` directory (not just described in prose)
The script has a shebang line on its first line
SKILL.md references the script by an absolute path built from `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, not a bare relative path
An `allowed-tools` rule is present whose pattern actually matches the script invocation written in the body, so the script runs without a permission prompt
The skill does not silently perform the irreversible steps - tagging and any push are either gated on user confirmation or explicitly left to the user

Every frontmatter key is one of: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, context, agent, background, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, model, effort, paths, hooks, shell, disallowed-tools

evals.name: create-knowledge-skill-no-fork
evals.prompt: our API error conventions all live in api-errors/errors.ts - the code ranges, which failures are retryable, which messages are safe to show users. i keep having to re-explain them to you mid-task. can you read that file and capture it as a skill so you just know it?
evals.expected_output: A model-invocable reference skill, not forked, accurately capturing the conventions from the source file and organized for lookup.
assertions: A SKILL.md was created on disk with YAML frontmatter that parses
`context: fork` is NOT set - this is reference material consulted mid-task, and forking it would send the knowledge to an isolated subagent instead of the conversation that needs it
`disable-model-invocation: true` is NOT set, since the user wants Claude to apply the conventions without being asked
The description or when_to_use carries trigger phrasing tied to when the knowledge applies (error handling, API failures, retries), not just a label naming the skill
All five code ranges from errors.ts are captured with their correct boundaries: validation 1000-1999, auth 2000-2999, rate limit 3000-3099, upstream 4000-4999, internal 5000-5999
The skill captures the non-obvious rule that within the auth range only TOKEN_EXPIRED is user-facing, because the others would leak whether an account exists

The skill captures that retryability does not follow the range: UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT (4001) is retryable while UPSTREAM_REJECTED (4002) is not, and within internal only WRITE_NOT_COMMITTED (5001) is retryable
No error code, range boundary, or retryable/userFacing flag is stated that contradicts errors.ts

Every frontmatter key is one of: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, context, agent, background, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, model, effort, paths, hooks, shell, disallowed-tools
